title: RC low-pass filter
what: First-order passive filter: lets low frequencies through, cuts high ones at 20 dB per decade.
result: Cutoff (-3 dB) 1000.0 Hz for a 1 kHz spec
-20.0 dB one decade above cutoff (20 dB/decade)

title: Sallen-Key low-pass filter
what: Second-order active filter (Butterworth, Q = 0.707) around the transistor-level op-amp: 40 dB per decade.
result: -3 dB at 9998 Hz for a 10 kHz spec, flat passband (peak 0.001 dB)
-40.3 dB one decade above cutoff (40 dB/decade)

title: Non-inverting amplifier
what: Amplifies by 1 + R2/R1 (here x10) with a high input impedance.
result: Gain 20.00 dB (x10.00) for a x10 spec
Bandwidth 1.12 MHz (spec: at least 100 kHz)
Phase margin 85° (stable)

title: LDO voltage regulator
what: Linear regulator: 5 V in, 3.3 V out at 0.1 A, using a PMOS pass transistor and an error amplifier.
result: 3.301 V out from 5 V in, at 0.1 A
Still 3.300 V at 3.6 V in (low dropout)
Phase margin 72°; load step dip 39 mV

title: Buck DC-DC converter (closed loop)
what: Switching step-down converter: 12 V in, 5 V out at 1 A, with a PWM controller that holds the output.
result: 4.999 V out from 12 V in, at 1 A, 500 kHz switching
Ripple 32.8 mV (limit 50 mV)
Efficiency 89.5%

title: Instrumentation amplifier
what: Three op-amps: amplifies the difference between two sensor wires by 100 and rejects what is common to both (mains hum).
result: Gain 40.00 dB (x100) for a x100 spec
Bandwidth 104 kHz (spec: at least 20 kHz)
Hum rejection (CMRR) at 60 Hz: 127 dB (spec: 80 dB)
Finished with standard 1% values; 0.1% resistors give 100% of boards in spec

title: Inverting amplifier
what: Amplifies by −R2/R1 (here −10).
result: Gain 19.98 dB (x−9.98), set by R2/R1 = 10
Bandwidth 191 kHz (op-amp sized for 2 MHz gain-bandwidth)

title: Common-source MOSFET amplifier
what: Single-transistor voltage amplifier.
result: Mid-band gain -2.0 dB (x0.80) from one MOSFET biased at 0.11 mA
Below a few Hz the source resistor cuts the gain to -2.8 dB; the 10 µF bypass capacitor removes that loss above it

title: Wheatstone bridge
what: Four-resistor bridge that turns a small resistance change (e.g. a strain gauge) into a voltage.
result: A 10% change in one arm gives 216 mV across the bridge at 10 V
Output is zero when all four arms match, and grows linearly with supply

title: Boost converter
what: Switching step-up converter: 5 V in, about 10 V out.
result: Steps 5 V up to 9.28 V (ideal at 50% duty: 10 V) into 50 Ω
Open loop: the output depends on the input; shows the drawer handles switchers

title: Two-stage amplifier with feedback
what: Two op-amps with an RC filter between them, one feedback loop around both, gain 10.
result: Gain 20.00 dB (x10.00), set by 1 + R2/R3 = 10
Feedback wraps both op-amps and the RC between them

title: Pi filter
what: C-L-C low-pass, as used on supply and RF lines.
result: Passband -6.1 dB (the 50 Ω source and load halve the voltage)
-82 dB at 100 MHz: steep 3rd-order roll-off

title: 5-stage RC ladder
what: Five RC sections in a row: a steep passive low-pass.
result: -3 dB at 13.2 kHz (each section loads the one before it)
-180 dB at 10 MHz: 100 dB/decade, five times one RC section

title: LC tank
what: Inductor and capacitor in parallel: resonates at one frequency.
result: Resonates at 5.01 MHz (1/2π√LC = 5.03 MHz)
Peak impedance 967 Ω, set by the 1 kΩ loss resistor

title: Two-stage CMOS op-amp
what: The 8-MOSFET op-amp inside circuits 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 11: differential pair, current mirror, gain stage, Miller compensation.
result: Open-loop gain 87.5 dB
Unity-gain frequency 10 MHz for a 10 MHz spec
Sized from a target gain-bandwidth; used inside circuits 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11

title: Comparator with gate drive
what: The op-amp's two stages, fast, then two CMOS inverters (12 MOSFETs) that can switch a power MOSFET.
result: Output swings rail to rail (0 to 12 V) whenever in+ crosses in−
Tapered buffer (small then large inverter) drives a power MOSFET gate directly
This is the PWM block of the closed-loop buck (circuit 5)

title: Chua's chaotic circuit
what: The simplest electronic circuit that behaves chaotically.
result: Chaotic oscillator: L, two capacitors and a negative-resistance (Chua) diode
Simulated in LTspice; the output never repeats and traces a double scroll
More plots (bifurcation, butterfly effect) in the README gallery

title: Inverting amplifier (template)
what: Amplifies by −R2/R1 with a set input resistance; sized from gain, bandwidth and load.
result: Gain 20.00 dB (x−9.995) for a x−10 spec, input resistance 10 kΩ
Bandwidth 1.01 MHz (spec: at least 100 kHz); phase margin 86°

title: Band-pass filter
what: Multiple-feedback band-pass: passes a band around one centre frequency (here 1 kHz, Q = 5).
result: Centre gain -0.01 dB at 1 kHz for a 0 dB spec (peak -0.01 dB)
Response at the band edges -2.81 and -3.23 dB (−3 dB ideal, Q = 5); phase margin 90°

title: Current-sense amplifier
what: Low-side shunt and difference amplifier: turns a load current (here 0 to 2 A) into a voltage for an ADC.
result: 2.487 V out at 2 A for a 2.5 V full scale (error -0.53%)
Error at 10% of full scale -3.39% (op-amp offset); bandwidth 104 kHz

title: ADC driver
what: Op-amp buffer and RC kick-back filter that settles a sampling ADC's input to half an LSB in time.
result: Settles to 0.06 LSB of its final value within the acquisition time after a 2 V step (spec: half an LSB)
Overshoot 0.00 LSB; fixed offset -0.40 LSB (the op-amp's); phase margin 87°

title: Bandgap voltage reference
what: Two transistors whose temperature drifts cancel: a steady voltage (here 2.5 V) from −40 to 85 °C.
result: 2.4995 V at 25 °C for a 2.5 V spec
Drift 13.3 ppm/°C from −40 to 85 °C (spec: 50 ppm/°C)

title: Input protection
what: Schottky diode against a reversed supply plus a TVS clamp against surges, in front of a 12 V load.
result: Clamps a 40 V surge to 16.7 V (load max 20 V)
Drops 0.74 V at 0.5 A; reversed input gives -0.001 V at the load

title: Boost converter (closed loop)
what: Switching step-up converter: 5 V in, 12 V out at 0.5 A, with soft start and a duty limit.
result: 11.997 V out from 5 V in, at 0.5 A, 300 kHz, closed loop
Ripple 80 mV (limit 100 mV); efficiency 94%; phase margin 88°

title: Flyback converter (closed loop)
what: Transformer-based converter: 12 V in, 5 V out at 1 A, with an RCD clamp on the switch.
result: 4.997 V out from 12 V in, at 1 A, 200 kHz, closed loop
Ripple 95 mV (limit 100 mV); switch sees 29.4 V with the RCD clamp (limit 60 V); phase margin 87°
